answer: An agent network can require each identity to earn a proof-of-work token by solving a hash puzzle over a fresh nonce and its public key; peers verify the answer cheaply. The nonce prevents replay, and key-binding stops one token being copied across accounts. A cipher may hide the challenge, or it may arrive as a whisper, but neither removes the cost: an attacker creating many identities must spend computation and energy for each, limiting how much influence they can buy by dawn.
